what: Analysis 1: Physical activity and systolic blood pressure in NHANES
title: Project proposal
text: Research question. Among US adults aged 40 , leisure-time physical activity relate systolic blood pressure? Unit analysis population. unit individual survey participant. population adults aged 40 NHANES data frame NHANES R package (2009-2012 survey cycles). use NHANESraw survey weights making population-level statements. Exposure. PhysActive (yes/participation moderate vigorous activity) primary exposure, coded two-level factor. PhysActiveDays (days per week) secondary, ordinal exposure. Participants missing exposure excluded primary analysis; tabulate missingness age, sex race compare complete-case result multiple-imputation analysis. Outcome. BPSysAve, average systolic readings, mm Hg. continuous. Confounders. Chosen looking data: age, sex (Gender), race (Race1), BMI, smoking status, education household income. also examine age--sex interaction use splines non-linear effects age BMI. Methods. Descriptive tables plots, linear regression adjustment confounders , survey-weighted estimates comparison. Limitations discussed include cross-sectional design, self-reported activity, lack antihypertensive medication information extract.

what: Analysis 2: State firearm legislation and firearm mortality
title: Project proposal
text: Research question. US states restrictive firearm legislation lower firearm death rates? Unit analysis population. unit state-year, 50 states D.C. years covered datasets. Exposure. gunleg (RAND State Firearm Law Database) construct, state year, cumulative number restrictive provisions effect cumulative number permissive provisions effect, using effective dates interpretive categories data. Provisions missing effective date unclear restrictive/permissive classification reported excluded counts, sensitivity analysis includes . Outcome. age-adjusted firearm death rate per 100,000 population cdcfiremort (CDC NCHS). continuous. Homicide rates cdcmurd used secondary outcome. Confounders. Census region division (datasets::state.region state.division), calendar year, state population. state fixed-effects model account time-invariant differences states. Methods. write R functions turn legislation records tidy state-year table, use time-series plots, maps, regression mortality legislation counts state year effects. Limitations discussed include ecological design, crude nature provision counts, reverse causation (states may legislate response rising mortality), differences years covered two sources.
